items.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: And I played this festival and this band was Andrew Hill, Bobby Hutcherson, Ron Carter, Roy Hanyes, Joe Henderson and myself.

ctx.x: When you grew up, I mean you obviously had the influence of your father, but there was certainly lots of pop music and so forth going on at the same time. Which of it caught your attention first?

Well naturally, like any kid, teenager, you grow up listening to the music that you grow up listening to, so I was no different. So at first it was R&B, rhythm & blues, all the singing groups, because I actually sang in a singing group. I had my own singing group. I sang in a few — did all the talent shows in high school. So I was listening to R&B, which would be Motown and the Drifters and things like that. Coming from Chicago, there was groups like the Impressions, Curtis Mayfield, Jerry Butler, you know the…
they’d be rehearsing with my dad and his bands. Don Baldwin, Andrew Hill, Vernel Fournier.
